title: Config Safety Layer: automated revert orchestration and audit-safe reconciliation
creator: Priya Karan
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, audit-friendly rollback orchestrator for runtime and routing configuration changes (batching/caching profiles, model routing, autoscale knobs). The system must detect safe-to-apply regressions, trigger fast automated reverts on defined failure modes, and reconcile controller state across control plane, Dedicated nodes, and Private deployments.

Scope and constraints:
- Triggers: metric threshold breaches (error rate, latency P95, tail latency increase), capacity exhaustion, cost spike (>10% token-cost deviation), and operator aborts.
- Guardrails: allowlist of config keys that can be auto-reverted, rate-limits on auto-reverts (max 1 per 10m per customer), dry-run simulation before apply where possible, and minimum successful-canary window.
- State reconciliation: eventual-consistency reconciler to detect drift between desired config and actual runtime state (KV cache placements, batching strategy, kernel flags). Reconciler must be idempotent and resume from last-applied operation.
- Observability: emit structured audit events for every config apply, reconcile action, and rollback with links to GitHub PR, changelist id, and console trace ids. Provide per-tenant rollback dashboard and a timeline view in the Console.
- Safety model: two-phase canary for non-critical and three-phase for high-impact changes (canary -> ramp -> global). Automated rollback allowed during canary and ramp phases if thresholds breached; after global, only operator-triggered rollback unless catastrophic SLO violation detected.

Deliverables:
1) Rollback orchestrator service with API endpoints: /apply, /status, /reconcile, /revert.
2) Canary engine integration with traffic routing to dedicated pools and metrics hooks.
3) State reconciliation worker with checkpointed oplog for resilient resumption.
4) Console UI additions: rollback timeline, one-click revert, root-cause hints.
5) Playbook & runbook for on-call and SEs describing modes, thresholds, and manual override steps.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We prioritize detection speed and safe automation over full automation coverage: only a conservative allowlist of config changes will be auto-reverted initially to limit blast radius.
- Oplog-based reconciliation chosen over periodic full dumps to minimize reconciliation cost and provide mutation-level provenance.
- Locking strategy: optimistic with compare-and-swap on revisions to avoid cross-region deadlocks; choose eventual consistency because some Private deployments cannot tolerate synchronous global locks.

Key success metrics:
- Time-to-detect regression < 2 minutes for latency SLO breaches.
- Time-to-revert (auto) < 3 minutes after trigger.
- < 0.5% false-positive auto-reverts in production during the quarter.

Links & artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CFG-rollback-orchestrator (internal)
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CfgRollbackDesign (architecture diagrams, canary flow)
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512 (orchestrator api + reconciler skeleton)
- Example dashboard (alpha): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollback-alpha/rollback-timeline

Open questions:
- Should cost-spike triggers use absolute token-cost delta or normalized per-model baseline? (proposal: normalized by recent 24h baseline per model + tenant)
- What retention period for audit events is required by security/compliance teams for Private deployments? (ask Security & Compliance)
- How to surface 'why revert' to customer-facing logs without exposing internal heuristics? (limit message to summary codes and link to console trace)

Next steps (this cycle):
- Build reconciler oplog prototype and run against sandboxed dedicated pool (Liam).
- Wire basic metric triggers from telemetry to simulate rollback decisions (Anjali).
- Iterate on allowlist and guardrail table with PM and Security (Marco, Priya).
